clue.text: Ball in the box pushed back Hearts regularly — they put a cross in the box

definitions.text: they put a cross in the box

indicators.note: pushed back means made to run the opposite way, so the letters are read from the end
something in something else sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the box is slang for the television
a ball is round, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A football commentary: the ball in the penalty box, Hearts pushed back, and players putting in crosses.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture misleads: the first box is the television, the second a ballot box. Hearts is a Scottish football club.
explanation.definitionFit: At an election people mark a cross beside their choice on a ballot paper, so this describes those who cast a vote.

clue.text: Following vehicle, I'm going to American plain

parts.note: a van is a road vehicle
I'm going to means I will, contracted to I'll
A is the standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Someone trailing behind a vehicle announces they're going to an American plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' simply places the vehicle at the start; 'plain' looks like a prairie but is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is used figuratively for anything ordinary or unadorned, the basic standard version with no extras.

clue.text: Appetising, pleasantly warm bagel's put away

indicators.note: put away means removed and stored out of sight, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: toasty means comfortably warm
a bagel is ring-shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A warm, appetising bagel has been eaten up.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the O from TOASTY to leave TASTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tasty has a pleasant flavour, so it is appetising to eat; the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Issue Guardian looks after, after dealing with wages, say

indicators.note: after says the phrase before it is placed later, behind the phrase that follows

parts.note: re means concerning or dealing with
issue means offspring, and wards are children in a guardian's care

explanation.surface: The Guardian newspaper covers an issue about pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the second piece after the first; Guardian is the newspaper in the surface but a legal guardian in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Wages are an example of payment received for work done, hence the 'say' marking an example.

clue.text: Anti-Congress, like one Republican force from the right

indicators.note: reading from the right is reading backwards in an across entry

parts.note: to dig is slang for to like
Roman numeral one
standard abbreviation
F is the symbol for force in physics

explanation.surface: A political jab at a Republican force opposing the US Congress from the right wing.
explanation.walkthrough: Congress here means sexual intercourse, not the US legislature, so anti-Congress means unwilling to have sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigid describes a person averse to sexual intercourse, a sense of congress found in older usage.

clue.text: One may be taken to court for fraudulent scheme

definitions.text: One may be taken to court
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bat strung for tennis or squash, carried onto the court
second meaning: a dishonest way of making money

explanation.surface: Someone is prosecuted in court over a scam.
explanation.walkthrough: The court looks like a law court, but it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the strung bat used in tennis and an illegal moneymaking operation.

clue.text: Ruler, say, put up with endless orgies, wild ones …

indicators.note: endless means without its final part, so the last letter goes
in a down entry, putting something up means writing it from bottom to top

parts.note: e.g. means for example

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: the word with its last letter removed
two Roman numeral ones

explanation.surface: A monarch tolerates wild orgies, the ellipsis carrying the scene into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is not a hint of example here but the letters for it; the ellipsis links to the next clue for surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: George the Third was King of Great Britain from 1760 to 1820, a monarch.

clue.text: … covered in oil perhaps, not naked

definitions.meaning: first meaning: with a salad dressing poured on

explanation.surface: Continuing the orgy, someone is oiled up but still clothed.
explanation.walkthrough: The oil suggests a body at an orgy; it is a salad.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad with oil on it has a dressing, and a person in clothes is clothed: one word for both.

clue.text: Two football teams without arrogance among stars

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: Inter Milan and Real Madrid, two clubs known by their short names
side is an old word for pretentious, swaggering manner

explanation.surface: Two football teams playing without arrogance among star players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' seems to mean lacking, but it means outside: the two clubs go round SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Interstellar space lies between the stars; sidereal relates to stars, so this means situated among them.

clue.text: Paper round, flipping burden!

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A frustrated paperboy curses his delivery round as a burden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British curse but signals the turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a duty or responsibility one must bear, which is a burden.

clue.text: Women imprisoned smuggling energy drinks chill here

parts.note: standard abbreviation

indicators.note: smuggling means carrying something secretly within, so one piece is tucked inside another

parts.note: in the cooler is slang for in prison
symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Female prisoners smuggle energy drinks to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: The cooler is slang for a prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine cooler is a container where bottles are kept cold, a place where drinks are chilled.

clue.text: Promiscuous person's soft blanket

parts.note: p for piano, soft in music
a blanket of snow, say, is a layer

explanation.surface: A womaniser's soft blanket on the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Player is informal for someone who has many casual sexual partners.

clue.text: Add ginger to fried greens I braise at the end

indicators.note: frying cooks things and changes them, so the letters are mixed into another order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at the end points to the final letter of the word before

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: spice fried greens with ginger before braising.
explanation.walkthrough: Ginger in the surface is the spice; as a verb, to ginger up means to enliven.
explanation.definitionFit: To ginger means to put spirit or vigour into, which is to invigorate or pep up.

clue.text: Isn't fat novel entertaining like Don Quixote?

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement
entertaining guests means having them inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: the letters rearranged
as means like

explanation.surface: Isn't a fat novel like Don Quixote entertaining?
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' points to Cervantes' long book, but it is the anagram signal; 'like Don Quixote' wants to be the definition, but 'like' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Quixote lives in a dream world of chivalry and tilts at windmills, the classic example of a dreamer.

clue.text: Parisian is hosted by ignorant society in backwater

indicators.note: a guest hosted by someone is held within their home, so one piece sits inside the others

parts.note: thick means stupid
est is French for 'is', as a Parisian would say it
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A Parisian is entertained by a boorish society in a provincial town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian is' gives the French word for 'is', inserted into THICK, with S added.
explanation.definitionFit: The sticks is informal for remote rural areas, far from towns: a backwater.

clue.text: New free houses in part of Lancashire, say

indicators.note: something that houses another holds it inside

parts.note: to rid is to free
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: New free housing is being built in a Lancashire district.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire is an English county, but here it is Lancashire cheese, which has an outer skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancashire is an English cheese, and the hard outer coating on a cheese is one part of it.

clue.text: Outstanding header from Spurs' subs

parts.note: due means owed, still outstanding

indicators.note: a header is what comes at the top, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A brilliant headed goal from a Tottenham Hotspur substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur football club; subs are not substitutes but subscriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: Subs is short for subscriptions, membership fees paid regularly, which are the dues of a club.

clue.text: Call evidence of overspending unconvincing

parts.note: to dub is to name or call
IOUs are notes acknowledging debt

explanation.surface: Claiming that something is evidence of overspending is unpersuasive.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubious means doubtful or questionable, not convincing to the listener.

clue.text: Suspected mug has funny diet drink's last bit in it

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters are put into a strange order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its closing stretch of letters

parts.note: its last three letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dodgy cup holds an odd diet drink's last dregs.
explanation.walkthrough: Mug is the face, not a cup: the diet letters are shuffled with the end of drink, then IT follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An Identikit is a composite picture of a suspect's face built from witness descriptions; mug is slang for face.

clue.text: Figure bags honour with ecstasy, one up for award

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it inside a sack, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a number, a figure
Order of Merit, a British honour
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A public figure lands an honour and is thrilled to be shortlisted for a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is someone put forward as a candidate, up for a prize or award.

clue.text: Insinuates you can't believe what troublemaker says

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous creature
lies are untruths, not to be believed

explanation.surface: Insinuations are things a troublemaker says that you shouldn't believe.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as 'the troublemaker's untruths': IMP then LIES.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply is to suggest something without saying it outright, which is insinuating.

clue.text: How week begins with caviar for old president

parts.note: Monday, abbreviated, begins the week
caviar is fish roe

explanation.surface: A former president starting each week with caviar.
explanation.walkthrough: James Monroe was the fifth US president.
explanation.definitionFit: James Monroe served as President of the United States from 1817 to 1825, long ago.

clue.text: Where stockholders make a killing?

parts.note: surface reading: a stock exchange, where shareholders earn huge profits
setter's reading: farmers holding livestock, taking animals to be slaughtered

explanation.walkthrough: Stock is livestock and a killing is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaughterhouse is where farm animals, the farmer's stock, are killed for meat.

clue.text: Paper, Times you said, probing legislator's muddles

indicators.note: probing means poking inside, so these pieces go into another

parts.note: a Member of Parliament's, with the 's giving S
the i is a British newspaper
the multiplication sign

indicators.note: said signals spoken sound, so the letter that sounds like the word is used

parts.note: the letter sounds like the word

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper investigates a lawmaker's blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: Paper and Times both look like newspapers; only the first is.
explanation.definitionFit: Mix-ups are confusions or mistakes where things get jumbled, which are muddles.

clue.text: Images of Musk company with more cash, we hear

parts.note: X is Elon Musk's renamed social network

indicators.note: hearing is listening to sound, so the word is written as it is spoken

parts.note: a raise is a pay increase

explanation.surface: Pictures of Elon Musk's company getting richer.
explanation.walkthrough: X is Musk's name for the former Twitter.
explanation.definitionFit: X-rays are pictures of bones and organs made with radiation, which are medical images.

clue.text: Push bucket down, carrying tons without doubt

parts.note: to force is to push hard

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to bucket down is to rain heavily
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Pushing a bucket down a well while carrying heavy loads.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucket down is British slang for pouring with rain.
explanation.definitionFit: For certain is an idiom meaning definitely, beyond any doubt.

clue.text: Got off with appeal after case for acquittal

indicators.note: a case is the outer shell, so the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: its first and last letters
it is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A defendant was let off after an appeal and an acquittal.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom picture makes 'Got off' mean acquitted; it means got down from a horse or bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Alit is a past tense of alight, to step down from a vehicle or dismount.

clue.text: Windows components needing small series of tests

parts.note: standard abbreviation
the Ashes is the England–Australia Test cricket series

explanation.surface: Microsoft Windows software components needing a small series of tests.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the cricket Test series played between England and Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Sash windows have sliding frames called sashes, which are parts of the window.

clue.text: Developing this drained Steve Jobs

indicators.note: developing means changing into a new form, so the letters reshape

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: drained means emptied of its contents, so only the outside letters remain

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Developing this product exhausted Steve Jobs of Apple.
explanation.walkthrough: Steve Jobs, the Apple founder, hides the definition: jobs are robberies.
explanation.definitionFit: A job is slang for a crime, especially a robbery, so jobs are heists.
